observations: Photo shows two rectangular black power-bank style casings/batteries on the floor.
One unit has a taped/covered area on its surface (looks like damage or removed label).
No visible brand/model markings, no ports clearly shown, and no screen/indicators visible.
Seller text says “Scrap power banks for sale in Ibadan.”

claims.claim: Scrap power banks for sale in Ibadan.
claims.evidence: Seller’s words match the visible condition (taped/damaged-looking units) in photo 0.

risks.risk: Whether any of the power banks can charge/hold charge (scrap may be dead or unsafe).
risks.proof: Video/clip showing each unit charging a phone (plug in + phone charging indicator) and then a short discharge test.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / for scrap only.

risks.risk: Battery safety risk (swollen, leaking, or damaged cells) that photos can’t confirm.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of both units’ surfaces and edges (including any bulging), plus a photo of the label/serial area if present.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as scrap with no warranty.

risks.risk: Quantity and completeness (missing cables, missing internal parts, or only casings).
risks.proof: Photo showing all items included in the bundle laid out clearly, and a count of units.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the worst case: incomplete/unknown parts.

risks.risk: Authenticity/quality (could be generic cells or mixed capacities).
risks.proof: Photo of any printed capacity rating (mAh/Wh) and port labels; if none, open/inspection proof is needed.

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of each unit’s ports (USB output/input) and any label/capacity (mAh/Wh).
Send a short video showing one unit charging a phone successfully (and ideally a second unit).
Send close-up photos showing whether any unit is swollen, leaking, or cracked.
Confirm the exact number of power banks included and whether any chargers/cables are included.
response.reason: From the single photo, the items look like damaged/taped power-bank casings, but there’s no readable brand/model, capacity, or proof they work. Without that, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
